directions: Grow as a houseplant or shaded, humid patio container in bright, indirect light in moist, well-drained potting mix. Black Prayer Plant bears oval leaves in a deep, near-black olive-green marked with a row of silvery-white to pale green blotches along the midrib, the darkest and most dramatic foliage color among the commonly grown Maranta leuconeura varieties, and like all prayer plants the leaves fold upward at night and unfurl again each morning in a distinctive daily rhythm. Native to the humid forest floor of Brazil, it thrives in the higher humidity of a bathroom, kitchen, or terrarium-adjacent setting and struggles in dry indoor air, often developing crispy leaf edges without a humidifier or regular misting. Keep soil consistently moist but not waterlogged, avoid tap water high in fluoride or chlorine if leaf tips brown, and divide congested clumps in spring to propagate and renew vigor.
